rounds.fact: Nintendo's site in the early 2000s was promoting both the GameCube and Game Boy Advance simultaneously, an unusually broad two-console push even by Nintendo's standards.
Firefox launched in 2004 as a leaner alternative to a bloated Netscape, and its 'Download Day' campaign set a Guinness World Record for most software downloads in 24 hours.
IMDb started in 1990 as a hobbyist mailing list of movie trivia before becoming a website, and is still one of the oldest continuously running sites on the entire internet.
Xanga combined blogging with heavy profile customization and briefly rivaled MySpace in popularity among teens before losing ground in the mid-2000s.
Airbnb started in 2008 with the founders renting out air mattresses in their own apartment during a design conference, which is where the original name came from.
